Titel: Renewal of [PROJECT]’s Security Service Providers [YEAR]-[YEAR]

## Summary

The [PROJECT] Foundation ("Foundation") and [PROJECT] Governance Working Group ("CGWG") are submitting this Snapshot to seek community approval for a one-year renewal of [PROJECT] DAO's security service provider arrangement, covering all three providers that secure the protocol today, as described in the Foundation's forum proposal: "Renewal of [PROJECT]'s Security Service Providers [YEAR]-[YEAR]".

The package saves the DAO $341,000, or 17%, against what these same three services cost today. Combined spend today is $2,036,000 — $2,000,000 of DAO-funded security spend plus the $36,000 of ChainPatrol coverage the Foundation has been carrying since the DAO's own funding line for it lapsed. The renewal brings that to **$1,695,000**, and to **$1,395,000** annualised once the vCISO component comes off, a reduction of $641,000, close to a third.

This Snapshot asks the community to approve the renewal on terms materially consistent with the forum proposal, authorize CGWG to coordinate with the Foundation and relevant stakeholders to finalize the arrangements, and approve disbursement from funds administered under the Treasury Management Committee ("TMC") framework.

## Background

The current arrangement was selected through the Security Service Provider RFP the Foundation ran in mid-[YEAR], to which sixteen proposals were submitted. Delegates selected ChainSecurity & Certora as SSP at $1.75M annually, with monitoring and incident response carved out to zeroShadow under a separate $250,000 engagement, taking the DAO's security spend from roughly $4M annualised to $2M.

ChainPatrol sits outside that structure, and this proposal returns it to the DAO rather than adding it. It was engaged on the DAO's behalf in [YEAR] and funded from the Growth Program budget. When that programme was not renewed, the coverage would have lapsed along with the authorisation the DAO had just granted; the Foundation has carried the $36,000 a year directly since then so that it did not. The service, the scope, and the DAO's authorisation have been continuous throughout; only the payer changed.

The DAO held two one-year renewal options at the prior commercial terms. Rather than exercise them at $1.75M, the Foundation renegotiated both security engagements from open-ended continuous models into defined, measurable ones, with reported utilisation. That restructuring is the substance of this proposal.

## Cost

| Provider | Current term | Proposed renewal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ChainSecurity & Certora | $1,750,000 | **$1,324,000**, reducing to **$1,024,000** annualised if the vCISO component comes off |
| zeroShadow | $250,000 | **$335,000** |
| ChainPatrol | $36,000 (carried by the Foundation) | **$36,000** (returns to the DAO) |
| **Total** | **$2,036,000** | **$1,695,000**, reducing to **$1,395,000** annualised |


Coverage is mostly restructured rather than cut. The auditor allocation is smaller than last year's consumption because routine governance proposal review moves to zeroShadow, where it costs less. zeroShadow's scope grows to absorb it: $93,000 of new scope less $8,000 of savings on the services being renewed, a net increase of $85,000.

Of the ChainSecurity & Certora figure, $300,000 is the vCISO component. The Foundation retains the vCISO for now and is not committing to a transition during this term. It is charged monthly, so the DAO pays only for the months in which it is provided and any balance not drawn stays with the TMC.

The renewal term runs twelve months, from **[DATE] to [DATE]**, the day after the current funded term ended, so the renewal continues it without a gap. The three engagements have run to different anniversaries until now; this term brings them onto one.

## Scope of Engagement

Scope is described at a high level; detailed statements of work sit with the Foundation.

**ChainSecurity & Certora.** An annual allocation of auditor capacity that [PROJECT] directs across its own priorities — smart contract audits, formal verification, web2 security reviews, and security architecture advice — rather than a fixed schedule of deliverables. Surge capacity is available for periods of exceptional activity, which is how a V4 audit programme would be funded once V4 is audit-ready, without a mid-term renegotiation. Both firms continue to hold a signer seat on the community multisig. Terms secured: 58 audit weeks a year with unused weeks rolling over, monthly usage reporting, and V4 surge rates locked now.

**zeroShadow.** Continued operation of the [DATE] virtual Security Operations Center, incident response, monitoring maintenance across onchain activity and [PROJECT]'s front end, participation as an independent security signer in the DAO's multisig structure, and threat intelligence platform access.

The substantive change is that zeroShadow expands its coverage of governance proposal review. Proposal simulation and mitigation becomes a defined, separately scoped part of the engagement rather than something absorbed informally alongside monitoring, freeing auditor capacity for code. Routine proposal review therefore sits with zeroShadow, with ChainSecurity and Certora engaged on request where a proposal warrants auditor attention. Terms secured: incident SLAs of acknowledgement under 15 minutes and escalation within three hours; and 200 hours of engineering support, split 120 to the current protocol version and 80 to V4, with unused hours rolling over.

**ChainPatrol.** Unchanged. Real-time monitoring for brand impersonation, phishing domains, fake social profiles, and wallet drainers targeting [PROJECT], with takedowns across domains, app stores, and social platforms.

## Rationale for Renewal

**The cost has moved in the DAO's favour without a concession on coverage.** The DAO held contractual options to renew at $1.75M. It is instead being asked to approve $1,324,000 now and $1,024,000 on a steady-state basis for the audit and advisory mandate, alongside a monitoring engagement that has grown in scope but reduced overall cost.

**The track record of security service partners is good.** 92 proposals reviewed in the first six months with no execution-related incident, and the cadence maintained through proposal 603. Eleven protocol audits with every critical and high finding resolved before deployment. Five proposals stopped and corrected before a vote. Two live events — deUSD and the rsETH exploit — met with same-day emergency action, every step reviewed before execution.

**Protocol-specific context is expensive to rebuild.** The team holds the proposal decoding and simulation tooling, sits on the community multisig, and has run the multisig fire drills. Re-tendering a year after a sixteen-proposal competitive RFP would cost more in transition risk than it could recover in price. On ChainPatrol, restoring a $36,000 line the DAO already voted for is the correction of an accident of administration, not a new commitment.

## Funding and Process

This proposal follows the below timeline:

- **RFC period:** seven days, [DATE] through [DATE], with questions answered in the forum thread by the Foundation, CGWG, or the providers.
- **Snapshot vote:** three days, opening Wednesday, [DATE] at 12:00 PM ET and closing Saturday, [DATE] at 12:00 PM ET.
- **Funding:** on approval, the TMC will fund the required streams and administer back pay.

Consistent with the Woof Year 3 and Cactus renewals, funding will be disbursed from the pool administered under the TMC, subject to the onchain controls described in that framework. Upon approval, the TMC would fund the term through four separate streams, with the capital committed upfront:

- **ChainSecurity & Certora — $1,024,000**, excluding the vCISO component
- **vCISO — $300,000**, cancellable independently of the rest
- **zeroShadow — $335,000**
- **ChainPatrol — $36,000**

Funding each provider separately means the DAO can act on one engagement without disturbing the others, and carving the vCISO out means it can be stopped at the point the Foundation's own security leadership takes the function on, without touching the audit retainer underneath it. The portion accrued from [DATE] through the start of the streams will be released upfront as back pay for the trailing period, as was done for the Cactus renewal, with the remainder streamed over the rest of the term.

Each stream is cancellable by the Foundation after a 60-day notice and cure period, no further governance proposal is needed to exercise it, and any balance not yet streamed remains under TMC control. Because the streams are separate, a cancellation reaches only the provider concerned. Cancelling the vCISO stream on transition needs no cause or cure period, since it is a planned handover rather than a remedy.

A lapse in security coverage is not a risk the DAO should carry for the length of an onchain cycle. The engagements remain fully subject to the service levels and reporting obligations agreed with the Foundation, and ratification by Snapshot does not waive them.

## Approval Requested

By voting "For," the community approves the renewal of the ChainSecurity & Certora, zeroShadow, and ChainPatrol engagements on terms materially consistent with the Foundation's forum proposal, authorizes the CGWG and Foundation to finalize documentation and operational arrangements, and authorizes the applicable $1,695,000 in payments, or equivalent arrangement, to be funded from TMC-administered funds through the four streams described above.

For a complete reading of the proposal, visit the Foundation's forum post below.

## Voting Options

**For:** Approve the renewal and authorize funding from TMC-administered funds on the basis described above.

**Against:** Do not approve the renewal or the proposed funding route.

**Abstain:** Register no position on the proposal.

Note: This vote will pass if "Yes" votes reach at least 400,000 [TOKEN] and outnumber the "No" votes.

Auswahl: For / Against / Abstain

Titel: Banning projects identified in the high-severity Watchdog Program cases - APX Finance

# Abstract

The following case from the [Watchdog Program]([URL] has been deemed to constitute high-severity misuse. Accordingly, the Watchdog Committee is proposing to ban this project from the ArbitrumDAO:

-   [APX Finance]([URL] (formerly ApolloX)
    

# Rationale

To strengthen oversight of grant allocations by the DAO and reduce misuse, the ArbitrumDAO approved the [Watchdog Program]([URL] to reward verifiable reports of misused funds. As of [DATE]; 90 reports have been submitted to the program, ~532K [TOKEN] has been recovered, and ~268K [TOKEN] has been distributed for reporter bounties.

### What constitutes a high-severity misuse?

As per the original Watchdog Proposal, high-severity misuse involves large-scale, deliberate misuse of DAO-allocated funds, including but not limited to fabrication of deliverables and theft.

As mentioned in the [Watchdog Retrospective Report]([URL] the Watchdog Committee (comprising Entropy Advisors, MinistroDolar, the [PROJECT] Foundation, and the OpCo) has deemed the following case to constitute high-severity misuse:

### APX Finance (formerly ApolloX)

**Rationale: Unreturned Funds + Late Distribution + Suspected Self-Sybil during** [**LTIPP**]([URL]

On-chain analysis uncovered multiple overlapping forms of misuse totaling 239,714 [TOKEN]. A substantial portion of LTIPP funds remained unutilized in the team's treasury addresses compared to distributor contracts as well as late distributions to said distributor contracts. Lastly, there was on-chain evidence linking a sybil cluster to team addresses.

The committee was unable to reach any team members for clarification or recovery.

# Steps to Implement

Before raising this proposal to an off-chain vote, this project had 1 week to present their case to the ArbitrumDAO as a reply on [this thread]([URL]

Unfortunately, the ArbitrumDAO did not receive a response from this project and the respective funds were not returned. Accordingly, the Watchdog Committee is seeking a vote from the ArbitrumDAO on the following:

-   Should APX Finance (formerly ApolloX) (including all founders, current team members, and affiliated contributors), be permanently banned from all future ArbitrumDAO programs?
    

The ArbitrumDAO will have the following voting options to choose from:

-   FOR - Ban APX Finance from the ArbitrumDAO
    
-   AGAINST - Do not ban APX Finance from the ArbitrumDAO
    
-   ABSTAIN
    

This proposal will not require an on-chain vote because there are no on-chain actions to be taken. Accordingly, this Snapshot vote aims to get social consensus from the DAO, and will serve as the final decision.

# Timeline

The following dates are tentative and subject to change.

1.  [DATE]: Publish proposal to the forum.
    
2.  [DATE]: Deadline for projects to respond.
    
3.  [DATE]: Publish off-chain vote to Snapshot.
    

If the DAO votes to ban this project, then the respective project will be ineligible to apply for any ArbitrumDAO programs going forward.

Auswahl: FOR - Ban APX Finance / AGAINST - Do not ban APX Finance / ABSTAIN

Titel: [PROJECT] ecosystem direction proposal

This proposal asks the [TOKEN] community to decide the fundamental direction of the [PROJECT] ecosystem.
After reading a lot of "suggestions"
The community must choose whether to:

Option A: Preserve and Rebuild the [PROJECT] Vision

Continue building the multi-token [PROJECT] ecosystem in which [TOKEN], BONE, LEASH, TREAT and SHI each have separate purposes, beginning with launch of LEASH V2 (it is ready to be launched).

Option B Simplify and Consolidate the Ecosystem

Move away from the existing multi-token structure and develop a plan to consolidate BONE, LEASH, TREAT and other ecosystem functions into one unified token or governance asset alongside [TOKEN].

This proposal selects a direction and if there is any change needed in future then it will happen.

Current Starting Position

Regardless of which option is selected, the community must proceed under the following assumptions and reality:

There is no access to an existing [PROJECT] treasury. In case they did then it should be transferred here [ADDRESS]
There is no guaranteed transfer of funds or holdings from previous ecosystem controllers.
**There is no guaranteed liquidity available for LEASH V2 so whoever wants to add liquidity anyone is free to do so. **
There is no development budget. Any product will be created will have fees (should be explained why and where and how much, everything on chain transparent nothing hidden) as explained before. Any products that will be launched will be owned by me currently since I do not not see any other proper solution for now and an action should be taken rather than waiting or doing nothing. Some have reached but I repeat any developer is free to reach me out. Any product should be audited before launch.
The community is effectively rebuilding from zero just how we started in [PROJECT] before.

Any development, liquidity or operational support must therefore come from transparent voluntary participation, new contributions, community builders or future revenue.

Option A Preserve and Rebuild the Original [PROJECT] Vision

Under Option A, the community affirms that the [PROJECT] ecosystem should continue as a collection of assets with distinct purposes.

The proposed structure would remain generally aligned with:

[TOKEN]: The flagship ecosystem token.
BONE: N/A for now
LEASH V2: A rebuilt version of LEASH and same utility as before such as exclusivity for early access and store of value and govern over SHI.
TREAT: to be discussed later but a reward token with unlimited supply (producing more when it is needed only controlled by a known multisig and known people in community not random voted by DAO to be part of that multisig and same goes for the management of future treasury but this is early to happen at current stage).
SHI: A future [PROJECT] ecosystem stablecoin.
new chain: super far in future and very early to even think about now
Keep in mind a lot of supply of current bone and treat is still controlled under shy and kaal and they keep dumping it until now even recently. So future migration is highly possible especially TREAT at current stages.

You can imagine all tokens move as a flywheel that benefit each other directly or indirectly such as burns (not fan of but many do think it is a must) or buybacks or whatever through products what will be built or rebuilt for example shibaswap (I will not accept launching just a random useless swap, it should be unique or something that can compete with others in the market at least a lesser fee for swapping for example, this is just an example when a project or product will be built to benefit [PROJECT]). The best focus now is to launch products that give utility for [PROJECT] and generate revenue for it. It is a step by step and need a lot of patience.

First Step: LEASH V2

If Option A is selected, LEASH V2 will be launched first rebuilding project.
It will be same as original supply 107646.4693.
How it works?
This contract is a non-rebasing wrapper for the original LEASH token. When you wrap your legacy LEASH, the contract locks your tokens and mints an equivalent amount of the new LEASH based on the legacy token's underlying gons accounting system. It is a separate ERC20 that can be traded anywhere just like any other token such as [TOKEN]. Because the conversion is based on gons rather than the displayed token balance, your proportional ownership is preserved even if the legacy token rebases.

The wrapped LEASH itself never rebases. Your wallet balance stays fixed, making it much easier to use with wallets, exchanges, and DeFi protocols that expect a standard ERC-20 token.

Example 1: If you wrap 100 legacy LEASH today, those 100 tokens are locked in the wrapper contract and you receive the equivalent amount of new LEASH. Your new LEASH balance remains constant, it will not automatically change because of future rebases from legacy LEASH.

Example 2: If the legacy LEASH supply later doubles due to a rebase or other supply change, your wrapped LEASH balance still stays exactly the same. If you decide to unwrap later, the contract calculates the redemption using the new current legacy supply, ensuring the conversion reflects the latest state of the underlying token.

You are free to move between the two versions whenever you choose. You can wrap legacy LEASH into the new token or unwrap back into the legacy token** at any time** for example because there is a better liquidity in legacy leash you can move there and sell at any moment or when you want to buy, provided the wrapper contract holds your deposited legacy LEASH. No one is forced to migrate, and no one is required to burn their legacy tokens. Wrapping is entirely optional and they can move on or back anytime they want and the contract will do the calculation by itself regardless if you move now or in the future you will not have any advanatge on anyone.

The contract is intentionally simple and has no owner, no admin controls, no transfer taxes, no blacklist, and no hidden mint function. The only way new wrapped LEASH can be created is by depositing legacy LEASH into the wrapper, and the only way wrapped LEASH is removed is when it is redeemed for the underlying legacy LEASH that was previously locked in the contract.

Auditing (suggest which company) it can be funded by the community to this current address
[ADDRESS]

Benefits of Option A
Preserves the established [PROJECT] ecosystem vision.
Gives existing ecosystem communities a possibility of continued utility.
Avoids abandoning the identities of the tokens.
Allows specialized tokens to support different ecosystem functions.
Provides a path to begin rebuilding through LEASH V2.

Risks of Option A
Multiple tokens may divide liquidity and attention.
Each token requires a credible purpose, developers and adoption.
Existing reputational problems may continue especially after the hacks and other previous histories. People should not expect refunds or any kind of that because it does not seem realistic at all if we are all being honest about it.
New liquidity may be insufficient.
The ecosystem may become too complex and a burden.

Option B: Simplify and Consolidate the Ecosystem

Under Option B, the community agrees that the existing multi-token structure should not be rebuilt in its current form.
In case B vote wins then
A later restructuring proposal would evaluate combining the intended functions, communities and possible obligations of BONE, LEASH, TREAT and related ecosystem assets into one unified token or governance asset. Which means there would be a direct forced burn migration except for [TOKEN] since it is pure and no need to do anything with it.

[TOKEN] would remain the central [PROJECT] token. The consolidated token could potentially provide governance, network incentives, access, ecosystem rewards or other functions

The exact structure and supply % and how much, would require another discussion.

Benefits of Option B
Simplifies the ecosystem.
Concentrates development and community attention.
Reduces competition between ecosystem tokens.
[MONTH] concentrate available liquidity.
Could provide one clear governance and utility structure.
Allows the community to redesign the ecosystem from zero.

Risks of Option B
Abandon the original [PROJECT] ecosystem vision.
Could damage existing BONE, LEASH and TREAT holders who refuse to move.
Fair conversion ratios may be impossible to determine.
A new token could appear to be an unnecessary fundraising mechanism to many.
Consolidation cannot automatically eliminate existing liabilities.
Lack of treasury access would still remain.
Creating another token does not guarantee demand, liquidity or adoption.

Auswahl: A / B / Abstain

Titel: [PROJECT] Alliance BORG Update: Appointment of Bryce Howarth as a New Director

## TL;DR

This vote seeks [PROJECT] DAO approval for the appointment of Bryce Howarth as a director of [[PROJECT] Alliance BORG Foundation]([URL] (“[PROJECT] Alliance BORG”).

Bryce is a professional independent director at [Horizons Global]([URL] He is a Chartered Accountant with extensive experience providing directorship, governance, compliance and operational support to protocol and foundation companies.

## Background

[PROJECT] Alliance BORG is a Cayman Islands foundation company established to support the purposes assigned to it under its governing documents as approved by [PROJECT] DAO. It has no members or beneficiaries, and its business and affairs are managed by or under the control of its board of directors. It is funded through [the Ecosystem Grant gRequest (EGG)]([URL]

Under the [[PROJECT] Alliance BORG Bylaws]([URL] as [amended]([URL] the foundation must have at least two directors, and director elections require approval by both the board and a Community Module Approval, i.e., approval by [TOKEN] holders via Snapshot vote.

## Proposal

Approve the appointment of Bryce Howarth as a director of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG.

If this proposal is approved:

- Bryce Howarth will be appointed as a new director of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG, with the board completing the necessary corporate actions to give effect to the appointment.
- Upon the appointment becoming effective, Adrian Cachinero Vasiljevic ([[HANDLE]]([URL] [[HANDLE]]([URL] will resign from his position as a member of the board.
- The board of [PROJECT] Alliance BORG will consist of Bryce Howarth and Shaun Musuka ([[HANDLE]]([URL]

## Rationale

Bryce Howarth is a professional independent director at Horizons Global, where he specialises in operational excellence for protocol and foundation companies. He provides hands-on leadership across governance, compliance and strategic planning for both early-stage projects and established protocols. He currently serves as an independent director of companies supporting a range of Web3 projects, including Layer 1 and Layer 2 networks, gaming platforms, yield infrastructure, real-world asset projects, decentralised exchanges and stablecoin initiatives.

Bryce is also a Chartered Accountant with a background in financial services. His combination of governance, operational and financial experience would strengthen the board's ability to support [PROJECT] Alliance BORG's activities and continued development.

Auswahl: For / Against

Titel: [PROJECT] DAO Proposal: Programmatic [TOKEN] Buybacks & Ecosystem Growth

## Summary

This proposal aims to achieve two main objectives

1.  Confirm the revenue contributed to the Foundation from Labs will be used to purchase [TOKEN] programmatically
    
2.  Denominate all user rewards in [TOKEN], primarily acquired on the open market, so that reward distributions are funded by purchases rather than new issuance.
    

The core principle of this proposal is to support the usage and adoption of the [PROJECT] protocol while continuing to build a sustainable treasury model for the [PROJECT] Foundation through a net accumulation of [TOKEN].

**Revenue contribution:**

[PROJECT] Labs will contribute monthly protocol revenue to the Foundation, which will use this revenue to buy [TOKEN] on chain via automated TWAPs pending this vote. The contribution of revenue from Labs will come from a share of the following revenue streams: interchange on card, swap volume, and staking revenue, which would’ve been ~$1.33M based on last month's numbers (subject to market conditions). Borrow revenue will also be included once total borrow volume reaches $50M (currently sitting at ~$250M in supplied capital in the market with $26M borrowed), along with other revenue lines in the future, which would include perps. These streams will be additive to the total as they ramp. Execution of these buys in the Foundation will not be discretionary, they will be programmatic. They will occur on a weekly cadence, resulting in linear buybacks of [TOKEN] over time.

**Mechanics:**

Moving forward, every reward on [PROJECT] will be paid in [TOKEN]. Here is an illustrative example: a user makes a $10,000 swap, which pays a $50 fee (50bps). That fee splits three ways:

| Fee leg | Share | $ on this swap | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Labs | 40% | $20 | Revenue to Labs to cover operating and infrastructure expenses |
| Buyback | 30% | $15 | Buys [TOKEN] on market, held in the Foundation treasury |
| User cashback | 30% | $15 | Buys [TOKEN] on market, delivered to the user as cashback |

Net effect of that one swap: $30 of [TOKEN] bought on chain, $15 of [TOKEN] shipped to the user. With this proposal, the result is a buy back of 30bps of volume, and a reward back to the user of 15bps, two tokens purchased for every one distributed. Perps and lending will run a similar split at their own fee levels.

Card cashback will be the same mechanism at a larger scale, paid in [TOKEN] acquired on the open market and funded from card revenue, staking revenue, and the fee funded buyback pool above, at rates the Foundation will set to target net [TOKEN] accumulation. The Foundation covers any remainder of [TOKEN] needed. It will do this by starting with a max of 20M [TOKEN] backup buffer which this proposal authorizes. This buffer comes from [TOKEN] the Foundation already holds. No new [TOKEN] is minted and circulating supply does not increase from this proposal. Rewards are funded first by on market purchases, meaning the program distributes [TOKEN] it has purchased. This top-up shrinks over time as the fee funded legs grow with volume and revenue.

The driving target of the program will be that [TOKEN] purchased by the Foundation on the market through revenue contributed from Labs meets or exceeds total [TOKEN] sold from distributions**.** We modelled this with conservative assumptions by assuming most cashback is sold immediately (which historically has not held true when looking at WETH distributed as cashback), and it runs near neutral even under this imperfect scenario. Membership staking, which the model excludes as a margin of safety, is what pushes it well into green. If net flow drifts negative, the Foundation can revisit the levers: cashback rates, fee splits, deployment pace. The dashboard published will outline [TOKEN] bought and [TOKEN] distributed.

![Buyback flow.png](ipfs://bafkreidexlykberh5xkr65pzihcw3nzrfuhdis6rluttmbd3bapb43e454)

Interchange settles in fiat, so the flow is collect and forward rather than a switch in a contract. Each week Labs aggregates the contribution, converts it to USDC, and sends it on-chain to a published Foundation address, and the Foundation will execute the buys as TWAP orders on CoW Swap. Both addresses will be published at launch, and the dashboard ties each week together: revenue reported, amount transferred, [TOKEN] bought. Any mismatch between a transfer and that week's revenue is visible on chain the same week.

**Further alignment through memberships:**

Building on this, and since the launch of [PROJECT] summer, staking [TOKEN] into account vaults is becoming a core path for users to gain membership benefits. The [TOKEN] a user earns as cashback now has an immediate use that rewards holding it. Spending earns [TOKEN], staked [TOKEN] improves membership, and better membership drives more spend by making the user's card top of wallet.

Since announcing the new membership structure, [TOKEN] staked in [PROJECT] account vaults has grown from roughly 21M [TOKEN] to 28M [TOKEN], an increase of ~7.2M [TOKEN] in fifteen days. We see a strong correlation with users choosing to accumulate [TOKEN] for membership, and none of that staking demand is counted in the net flow example above.

**Summary:**

Protocol revenue now translates directly into automatic [TOKEN] purchases in the Foundation, and the incentive budget grows the revenue that funds it. Rewards are paid in [TOKEN], largely paid from buys in market, and memberships gives that [TOKEN] a reason to stay within the app. Rewards are funded first by on market [TOKEN] purchases with a 20M [TOKEN] backup buffer from existing Foundation holdings, meaning no new [TOKEN] enters circulation. All discretionary decisions are removed: [TOKEN] purchase mandate is fixed, execution will be on chain, and the dashboard shows every dollar in and every [TOKEN] out.

**Vote**

FOR: Approve (1) ongoing Labs revenue contributions to the Foundation to be used for programmatic [TOKEN] buybacks via automated TWAPs, with purchased [TOKEN] held in the Foundation treasury or distributed as user rewards under the program described above; and (2) authorization of up to 20M [TOKEN] from the Foundation's existing treasury (no new [TOKEN] minted) to fund user rewards and ecosystem incentives, to be managed with the target of net [TOKEN] accumulation over time.

**AGAINST**: Do not approve.

Auswahl: For / Against / Abstain

Titel: [ARFC] Onboard PAXG to the Global Dollar Hub in [PROJECT] V4 Ethereum

### [ARFC] Onboard PAXG to the Global Dollar Hub in [PROJECT] V4 Ethereum
### Author: [PROJECT] Labs
### Date: [DATE]

***

## Summary

This proposal seeks to onboard Pax Gold (PAXG) to the Global Dollar Hub on the [PROJECT] V4 Ethereum instance. Final asset configuration will be determined by the Risk Service Providers.

## Motivation

PAXG is an ERC-20 token issued by Paxos Trust Company, where each unit represents one fine troy ounce of a London Good Delivery gold bar held in professional vaults. Redemption and custody are administered by a regulated issuer, and holdings are subject to periodic third-party attestations.

Onboarding PAXG to the Global Dollar Hub is aligned with the DAO's long-term objectives in several ways:

  - It introduces a gold-backed, real-world asset to the [PROJECT] V4 Ethereum instance, broadening the range of collateral and liquidity available beyond dollar-denominated exposures.
  - It gives users access to a regulated, physically-backed representation of gold within the [PROJECT] ecosystem, supporting demand from institutional participants and DeFi protocols seeking commodity exposure.
  - It complements the Global Dollar Hub's existing composition, adding a non-correlated asset that strengthens the instance's position as a venue for diversified liquidity strategies.

## Specification

This proposal adds PAXG to [PROJECT] V4 Global Dollar Hub in Ethereum

Token Address: [[ADDRESS]]([URL]


Likewise, adds PAXG as a collateral-only asset to a new Spoke named Gold Spoke. In parallel, to avoid additional governance proposals, enables native USDG as a borrowable reserve on the Pendle Spoke with a 4,000,000 USDG Draw Cap.

### Dynamic Liquidation Bonus Configuration

As a non-crypto open-market spoke, it merits more conservative liquidation restoration parameters. Draw Caps will be set conservatively to reflect the Gold Spoke’s still-developing borrow-side liquidity profile.

Spoke-level liquidation parameters:

| **Parameter** | **Value** | **Rationale** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| targetHealthFactor | 1.20 | Open-market non-crypto collateral dynamics require more conservative post-liquidation restoration to reduce reliquidation risk. |
| healthFactorForMaxBonus | 0.90 | Lower trigger avoids overpaying incentives too early while still reaching max LB before the deficit zone. |
| liquidationBonusFactor | 0.80 | Matches the Main Spoke baseline and preserves V3-equivalent Gold correlated asset bonus at HF~1 with a 1.25x max LB cap. |

### Spoke Parameters

| **Hub** | **Spoke** | **Reserve** | **Collateral Factor** | **Max Liquidation Bonus** | **Borrowable** | **Collateral Risk** | **Liquidation Fee** | **riskPremiumThreshold** | **receiveShares** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global Dollar Hub | Gold Spoke | PAXG | 75.00% | 6.50% | FALSE | 0 | 10.00% | 0 | TRUE |
| Global Dollar Hub | Gold Spoke | USDG | 0.00% | - | TRUE | - | - | 0 | TRUE |
| Global Dollar Hub | Pendle Spoke | USDG | 0.00% | - | TRUE | - | - | 0 | TRUE |

### Oracle

List PAXG against the Chainlink XAU/USD price feed, pricing the token at underlying gold spot with no CAPO growth-ceiling wrapper. PAXG carries no monotonic exchange-rate growth for a cap to bound, so a CAPO adapter is not recommended. The accepted risks are a sustained token-level dislocation priced at full gold spot and the feed’s weekend staleness. The liquidation parameters set at any future collateral-enable phase must absorb that envelope rather than assume a continuously updating reference.
